text:
maria: Heads-up — last night eu-west1 saw a spike of GPU pod evictions around 03:20 UTC. Evictions all blamed on node pressure but dig into kubelet logs and network metrics and it smells like sustained inter-node bandwidth saturation during large model loads.

aj: saw the same in alerts. pod eviction count + pod restarts on gpu-pool-3. Link to grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/GPU?panelId=7 (bandwidth) — egress saturated for a subset of nodes.

maria: exact symptoms: VNLink NIC counters at 95% for ~10m, RDMA peer-to-peer transfers stall, models hitting p2p fallback which spikes host-to-host traffic. Pods have strict nodeAffinity to gpu-type=hf; that cluster has tight binpacking.

kevin: do we have examples?

maria: here’s a compressed snippet from the kubelet logs on node gpu-eu-12: ```
I0320 03:20:12.345 kubelet_eviction.go:289] eviction manager: observed resource pressure: NetworkAvailable==false
W0320 03:20:15.112 eviction_manager.go:412] evicting pod user-model-123 due to ephemeral-storage pressure (host-network churn)
```

aj: interesting that it reports ephemeral-storage but correlates with NIC saturation. I think kernel qdisc is queuing and writes backpressure to pod IO paths.

kevin: hypothesis: tight GPU binpacking + zone-local affinity -> a few nodes become egress hotspots when multiple replicas perform weight-syncs / KV cache fetches. Eviction policy then misattributes root cause.

maria: agreed. Two lines to mitigate quickly: 1) add a network-aware scoring to scheduler to prefer spreading pods when expected egress > X; 2) relax strict affinity for non-latency-critical worker batches.

aj: for (1) we can prototype a scheduler plugin that uses a node metric 'node.network.egress_estimated' and penalizes nodes over threshold. Pseudocode: ```score := baseScore - clamp((egress - target)/scale, 0, 100)```

kevin: for (2) suggest adding a toleration/affinity label set for batch jobs: "gpu.alloc_class=batch" so we can run batch on a different compact pool with larger network headroom. Also suggest a runtime config to limit concurrent p2p fetch concurrency per pod.

maria: I created a quick kustomize patch for the scheduler feature gate and scoring plugin (POC, not prod): ```yaml
apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: KubeSchedulerConfiguration
profiles:
- schedulerName: default-scheduler
  plugins:
    score:
      enabled:
      - name: NetworkEgressScore
  pluginConfig:
  - name: NetworkEgressScore
    args:
      targetEgressMbps: 500
      scale: 200
```

aj: nice — can you add a gradual rollout? maybe start in dev and then canary the profile on a single pool.

maria: will do. Also opened infra ticket INFRA-4387 to add node exporter metric node_network_egress_estimated and a grafana alert.

kevin: rough cost question — if we start spreading more, we might need more inter-rack bandwidth or larger NIC SKUs. Estimate: moving 30% of batch traffic off the compact pool would require +40Gbps NIC on 8 nodes -> roughly $3k/mo additional. Still cheaper than repeated evictions during peak.

aj: operational play: short term, add eviction grace extension for gpu pods during nightly batch window (extend pod-eviction-grace to 30s) and throttle concurrency on workers. Long term, plugin + dedicated batch pool with network headroom.

kevin: I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to approve the canary plan. @sre-bot can you post the nightly eviction histogram into #eng-platform every morning until we close INFRA-4387? :thumbsup:

sre-bot: scheduled: daily report at 06:00 UTC to #eng-platform. source=infra-metrics, query=evictions_gpu_pod_count{region="eu-west1"}.

maria: thanks — plan: (a) canary plugin in staging, (b) add node metric + alert, (c) label batch workloads, (d) tweak eviction grace and worker concurrency.

aj: +1. logging follow-ups in INFRA-4387 and SCHED-219.

kevin: thanks all. I'll capture action items and owners in the ticket and we can finish the rollout next week. :rocket:
